note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 after 286bd6e63f removed {partial} (independent judge, clean clone at fa82653066). RFC 3948 Section 5.1: "Because SGW will now see two possible SAs that lead to 10.1.2.3, it can become confused about where to send packets coming from Suzy's server.  Implementors MUST devise ways of preventing this from occurring." The seven tagged units are sound for what they assert: TestRFC3948TwoUnboundPeersSameInnerAddressSecondRefused (second unbound peer on 10.1.2.3/32, TSr 0.0.0.0/0 vs 192.0.2.10/32: errTSUnacceptable, notify TS_UNACCEPTABLE, the 5.1 text, zero states and policies on b, a's two policies and one record kept), TestRFC3948TwoUnboundPeersDistinctInnerAddressesServed (10.1.2.3 and 10.1.2.4 both served, two policies, two records), TestRFC3948ConfiguredOverlapNarrowedByPeerRefused (peer-chosen narrowing inside a shared configured 10.0.0.0/8 refused), and the pool-bound TestTwoPeersSameRequestedAddressDistinctLeases, TestNoChildSAWithoutLeaseOnBoundPeer and both TestRFC3948ZeInitiatedRekeyNamesOnlyTheLease tags. ./le rfc discriminate id RFC3948-5.1-1: seven verified mutant records, none stale, none unproven; the tagged and sibling tests pass with -race. Removal paths read: every Child SA removal (peer Delete, rekey retire, supersede, DPD/lifetime/dead exits via cleanupChild, stale parallel handshake, cleanupPendingSA, stopPeerSession on reload/stop) reaches removeChildSAExcept, which releases first; MOBIKE and NAT rebind migrate endpoints only and keep the record; a failed install releases; claim re-checks under the registry lock. WHY WEAK: the tagged set cannot fail on the non-compliance that remains. conflictLocked (inner_selectors.go) exempts any overlap whose two remote halves are operator-fixed, at any policy-priority. Probe in the clone: peer a configured remote 10.1.0.0/16, peer b configured remote 10.1.2.0/24, both at the default policy-priority 2000, each negotiated whole: both served, outbound policies 0.0.0.0/0->10.1.0.0/16 and 0.0.0.0/0->10.1.2.0/24 both at priority 2000, two records. A packet to 10.1.2.3 matches both SAs and the SPD gives no order between them; the policy-priority YANG description says peers that share a value are ordered by whichever established last. That is the Section 5.1 confusion, reachable with the default priority on any two peers whose configured remote prefixes nest, and RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1's ordering exemption does not cover it because no order was configured. No tagged test covers that case, and TestInnerSelectorConfiguredOverlapNegotiatedWholeAllowed uses distinct priorities only. Fix: in conflictLocked keep the both-fixed exemption only when p.policy.Priority != h.policy.Priority, add a negative tagged test for the equal-priority case with its discrimination record, and correct the policy-priority YANG text and the Support remaining row. Until then the row's 'None for Section 5.1' overstates support.
